subject: sarf
definition: A verb whose root letters include none of the weak letters: wāw, yāʾ and alif.
explanation: نَصَرَ، ضَرَبَ، كَتَبَ are sound. Their letters stay as they are in every form, so their conjugation follows the patterns exactly.

Within the sound verbs the books separate the sālim (no hamza and no doubled letter, as نَصَرَ), the mahmūz (with a hamza, as أَكَلَ) and the muḍāʿaf (with the second and third root letters the same, as مَدَّ). The Nahwi's conjugation tool works on the sālim.

examples.english: kataba yaktubu: sound; every letter stays.
akala, he ate: sound, with a hamza (mahmūz).
